questions.question: How do you handle logout in SSO environments? What is session expiry vs active logout?
questions.title: SSO Logout & Session Expiry — Front-Channel vs Back-Channel
questions.direct_answer:
How do you handle logout in SSO environments? What is session expiry vs active logout?

**In one line:** name the mechanism, where it applies (the browser, network, and server contract (headers, cookies, streams)), and the user-visible outcome.

**Interviewers dig into:** Local logout (clear tokens); single logout (SLO) via front-channel iframe or back-channel OIDC; clearing SSO session at IdP.

**Classic weak answer:** Clearing local tokens but leaving the IdP session alive — the next login re-authenticates silently, surprising the user.

**Senior finish:** Explain front-channel vs back-channel logout in OIDC and why back-channel is more reliable.

sections.title: Why this question matters
sections.content:
This question — **SSO Logout & Session Expiry — Front-Channel vs Back-Channel** — shows up constantly in **frontend / fullstack** interviews because it separates candidates who memorized docs from candidates who can **reason about real systems**.

**Restate the prompt:** How do you handle logout in SSO environments? What is session expiry vs active logout?

A gold-level answer does four things in order:

1. **Define** the terms in plain English (what it is / what problem it solves).
2. **Explain the mechanism** (what runs when: browser, bundler, framework, network).
3. **Compare trade-offs** (speed vs correctness vs security vs DX) with **when you would not use** the default.
4. **Ground it in production** — caching, auth, observability, tests, or an incident you handled.

Interviewers are listening for: **Local logout (clear tokens); single logout (SLO) via front-channel iframe or back-channel OIDC; clearing SSO session at IdP**.

The fastest way to lose points is: **Clearing local tokens but leaving the IdP session alive — the next login re-authenticates silently, surprising the user**.

If you only add one “senior” layer, make it: **Explain front-channel vs back-channel logout in OIDC and why back-channel is more reliable**.

sections.title: Deep dive — what to say
sections.content:
### What to explain (middle of the answer)

- **Core mechanics:** Local logout (clear tokens); single logout (SLO) via front-channel iframe or back-channel OIDC; clearing SSO session at IdP
- **Concrete shape:** give a small code or config snippet *only if it clarifies* (5–15 lines max).
- **Interviewer follow-ups:** expect “what breaks in production?”, “how do you debug?”, “what would you measure?” — answer them proactively.

### How to sound senior (without rambling)

- Tie the feature to **user-visible outcomes** (performance, accessibility, security).
- Mention **one failure mode** you have actually seen (race, stale cache, hydration mismatch, flaky test).
- Close with **one decision rule** (“choose X when …; choose Y when …”).

sequenceDiagram

    participant I as Identity Provider
    participant B as BFF / API
    participant R as Resource API
    U->>I: Authorize (PKCE / code)
    I-->>U: Authorization code
    U->>B: Exchange code (server-side)
    B->>I: Token endpoint + client auth
    I-->>B: Access + refresh (optional)
    B-->>U: HttpOnly session cookie

sections.title: Trade-offs & senior signal
sections.content:
### Trade-offs interviewers expect you to name

- **Speed vs safety** (types, runtime checks, validation).
- **DX vs constraints** (framework magic vs explicit wiring).
- **SEO / first paint vs interactivity** (SSR/SSG/CSR choices where relevant).
- **Security vs convenience** (tokens, cookies, localStorage, third-party scripts).

### What “book answer” misses

- **Book answer:** repeats definitions.
- **Strong answer:** names **clearing local tokens but leaving the IdP session alive — the next login re-authenticates silently, surprising the user** and what you do instead.

sections.title: Key points (memorize this list)
sections.content:
- **Headline definition** in one sentence.
- **Mechanism:** Local logout (clear tokens); single logout (SLO) via front-channel iframe or back-channel OIDC; clearing SSO session at IdP
- **Pitfall:** Clearing local tokens but leaving the IdP session alive — the next login re-authenticates silently, surprising the user
- **Differentiator:** Explain front-channel vs back-channel logout in OIDC and why back-channel is more reliable
- **Proof:** DevTools / Network / Performance trace, test strategy, or metric.
- **Close:** decision rule + sensible follow-up question back to the interviewer.

sections.title: How to answer verbally (timed)
sections.content:
**Open (15–20 seconds):** Restate the question and give the one-sentence definition.

**Body (45–60 seconds):** Walk through **Local logout (clear tokens); single logout (SLO) via front-channel iframe or back-channel OIDC; clearing SSO session at IdP** as a story: what runs, what breaks, what you log/measure.

**Pitfall (15 seconds):** Call out **Clearing local tokens but leaving the IdP session alive — the next login re-authenticates silently, surprising the user** — interviewers reward honesty about real bugs.

**Finish (15–20 seconds):** Add **Explain front-channel vs back-channel logout in OIDC and why back-channel is more reliable**, then offer a trade-off question back (“do you optimize for TTFB or TTI here?”).
